_note: THE INPUT-ARM INVENTORY. One record per thing the original's interface responds to,
and one per thing OURS responds to that the original does not.
WHY IT EXISTS. docs/decisions.md C61: three screen groups were enumerated arm by arm
out of the decompilation and compared against our source, and we reproduced 80 of 185.
Every miss was a behaviour nobody had looked for, and three of them were inventions
rather than omissions. CLAUDE.md rule 5 came out of that measurement; this file is what
checks it, because a stated rule on this project does not hold and a checked one does.
THE CHECK, and it is the only thing everything else is arranged around:
the set of `id`s here with status "reproduced" is EQUAL, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, to the set
of `// arm: <id>` markers in the Rust. A record with no marker is a claim nobody kept; a
marker with no record is an arm nobody wrote down. crates/l2-game/tests/arms.rs is the
test and it names both differences.
THE MARKER. `// arm: 0xAAAAAAAA/slug` on its own line, immediately above or inside the
thing that implements it. The address is the ORIGINAL function the behaviour reproduces
-- not the painter of the screen it sits on -- and the slug disambiguates the several
arms one function can hold: FUN_0043BF07 alone is four of them. An id therefore starts
with `0x` and a marker is greppable as `// arm: 0x`.
STATUS, and there are five, because status is a CROSS-PRODUCT of two questions: what the
ORIGINAL has (live / dead / not at all) and what WE have (built it / did not). Five of the
six cells are named below; the sixth -- neither has it -- is not a record. They are one
field rather than two because these are the things anyone actually counts, and splitting
them would make every count a join for no gain in the common case.
reproduced -- we do it. MUST have exactly one marker.
missing    -- the original does it and we do not. The 1:1 gap.
dead       -- it is in the binary and cannot run. Not a gap: building it would be
reproducing code the shipped game never reaches. `why` says how that
was established, and it has to be an exhaustive check rather than a
failure to find.
invention  -- WE do it and the original does not. `removed` says whether it is still
in the tree. This is the direction C61 found three of and had no way to
count; an invention is worse than an omission because nothing looks
broken.
dead-reproduced -- we built an arm the shipped game cannot reach. Its own value, and
deliberately an awkward one, because it is a FINDING rather than a
category. It must not count in the 1:1 numerator, since no player can
reach it, and it must not hide inside `dead`, since we are carrying the
code. If one appears the likely right answer is to DELETE the code, not
to keep the record. MUST have exactly one marker, like anything we build.
So a marker is required exactly when we implement something: reproduced, invention or
dead-reproduced. `crates/l2-game/tests/arms.rs` holds that list in one place so the rule
cannot drift as statuses are added.
EVIDENCE is CLAUDE.md rule 4's: V verified against a second independent source, D a
straightforward reading of decompiled C, I inferred.
COUNTING. One (screen, gesture, guard) that a player can tell apart is one arm. A table
of N identical widgets hit-tested in one call is ONE arm (the menu bar's three titles,
the nine control-group keys); a ladder with N distinct outcomes is N arms (the overview
panel orders or looks: two). Where a count here differs from C61's, the counting rule is
the likeliest reason and the `group` totals in docs/battle.md section 15 say so.
COUNTED PER IMPLEMENTATION, NOT PER SCREEN. An arm live on three screens -- the overview
panel is -- is ONE record here, because the check compares this file against code and the
code has one function. docs/battle.md section 15.11 counts the same arms the other way,
once per screen, because that is how C61 counted and the two totals have to be
comparable: 33 records for 38 arms, and section 15.11 names the five that differ.
STATE OF THE FILE is in `groups` now, per group, as `complete`. A paragraph saying which
groups are finished goes stale silently; a flag the census can read does not.
GROUP is the unit somebody can claim COMPLETE -- an enumeration and its owner -- and not a
taxonomy of the interface. Any taxonomy is derivable from `screen`, so `group` carries the
thing that is not derivable: who enumerated this, and whether they finished. C61 measured
three groups, but those three were an artefact of how one evening happened to split across
three agents, which is the worst possible reason to freeze a taxonomy.

battlefield.note: Enumerated arm by arm from Screen_FrameInput, Screen_Draw and the window proc.

seam.what: 0x12 and 0x13, the prompt and the report either side of a battle
seam.note: 0x12 and 0x13 only. The rest of the campaign-side chrome is not in this file.

text.what: TYPING. Every text-entry field in the game, and the keyboard dispatch behind them.
text.note:
THE GAME HAS SEVEN TEXT FIELDS. Enumerated exhaustively and from the direction that cannot miss one: `g_editActive` (0x005AEB78) is the single flag that decides whether a keystroke reaches the edit buffer at all, Screen_HandleInput CLEARS it at the top of every frame, and exactly seven of its arms set it again. Every one of those seven is a record below, and there is no eighth because there is no eighth writer of the flag in the binary. A second enumeration from a different direction agrees, and closes exactly: Edit_Commit (0x0040210C) -- the OTHER end, where the buffer is copied out to wherever the field belongs -- also has exactly SEVEN call sites, and they are the same seven places, each one two lines below its `g_editActive = 1`. Four distinct destination buffers between them, because three of the seven share DAT_00553E80. (Edit_Begin, the third end, has 23 call sites over 14 seed strings, and is NOT a count of fields: a seed is the text a field opens with, and most of those 14 are string literals in .rdata.)

THE DISPATCH IS THE WINDOW PROCEDURE (0x004B29BE), not Screen_FrameInput and not Screen_HandleInput -- which is why an audit that read the screen ladders found no text entry to count. WM_CHAR (0x102) is one statement, Edit_TypeChar(ch), with NO screen test; the seven editing keys are WM_KEYDOWN (0x100) cases and are equally ungated. The whole editor is one 2000-byte buffer at 0x005CD550 with a caret, two limits and a kind, and the sixteen functions between 0x00401984 and 0x0040210C are all of it.

ARMS ARE COUNTED PER IMPLEMENTATION here as everywhere: the seven editing keys are ONE record each even though every field is edited by the same seven, because crates/l2-game/src/text.rs has one function each. The seven FIELDS are seven records because they are seven guards in seven places.

front-end-keys.what: The keyboard on setup screen 0x1F and the save/load box 0x35/0x36
front-end-keys.note: Recorded because enumerating the text fields meant reading these ladders anyway, and what it turned up is that THE FRONT END HAS NO KEYBOARD AT ALL in the original: not one of Screen_HandleInput's thirteen g_setupPage arms tests a key, and the window procedure has no g_screenId == 0x1F case. Every `ours/setup-*` and `ours/saveload-*` record below is therefore an invention, and they are KEPT rather than removed -- a menu a person cannot drive from the keyboard is worse, not more faithful. They are here so the count is honest, which is the whole point of the `invention` status.

arms.what: VK_RETURN IS THE SAVE/LOAD BOX'S CONFIRM BUTTON. Edit_Confirm's whole body is `g_saveLoadConfirm = 100`, which is the IDENTICAL assignment the confirm widget's own handler FUN_004342F3 makes, and SaveLoad_Tick (0x004AD9F0) reads that latch, builds the path and does the load or the save.
arms.note: Ours had Enter confirm this box as a convenience, unattributed. Reading the keyboard path turned it into an arm -- the one case in this group where a guess happened to be right, and it is worth as much as the ones that were wrong.

arms.what: VK_BACK: caret back one, THEN delete. Not gated on the field being full, which is what makes deleting the only way out of a field that has hit either limit.

VK_INSERT: g_editInsert ^= 1, and that is the whole function. It matters far more than the name suggests, because OVERWRITE IS THE DEFAULT -- see 0x00401D26/overwrite-default -- so this is the key that turns typing OVER the name you have into typing BESIDE it.
VK_LEFT: `if (0 < caret) caret--`. The window procedure's arm ALSO steps g_debugSelectedMan down, which is the battle debug panel's figure index and is the one debug key of the four that is ungated.
VK_RIGHT: `if (caret < length) caret++`. Stops at the length, not at the character limit.
VK_HOME: caret = 0.

VK_END: caret = length. The window procedure's VK_END arm calls TWO functions -- this and Chat_Close (0x004360F2) -- so the same key also cancels a pending save; see 0x004360F2/end-cancels-confirm, which is a separate record and is missing.

Edit_Insert has TWO branches with DIFFERENT limits and the wrong-looking one is the default. g_editInsert (0x005C9280) starts at zero, zero is the OVERWRITE branch -- `buf[caret++] = ch`, bounded only by the caret reaching the character limit -- and the insert branch additionally needs the LENGTH to be under it. So arriving on the name page, whose field is seeded with the name you already have, and typing E, d gives Edayer1 and not Ed. docs/bugs.md B79.
arms.note: Reproduced as found, not corrected. The caret glyph follows it and is the opposite way round to the usual convention: underline for overwrite, I-beam for insert.

arms.what: VK_DELETE, through 0x00401C93: the tail shifts left over the caret and the caret stays. More load-bearing than it looks -- see 0x00401D26/overwrite-default, where it is how a person gets from Edayer1 to Ed.

Edit_DrawCaret: a counter 0..=16 stepped once per call, drawn only above 8, so EIGHT FRAMES LIT IN SEVENTEEN. Two shapes: overwrite draws a 2-pixel underline under the character, insert draws a 15-pixel I-beam with four serifs before it. The underline's width is the advance of the character UNDER the caret, and at the end of the text that character is the terminator, whose advance FUN_004015B9 returns as 0 -- so the caret at the end of a name is a two-pixel stub.
arms.note: Not an input arm; recorded because it is the whole of the affordance -- there is no focus ring and no second plate frame, so a field with no caret is indistinguishable from a label, which is exactly what ours were. Ours steps on a TICK rather than a frame, because docs/netcode.md does not let anything below the renderer read a clock. Presentation only.

arms.what: Menu_OpenDropdown(&g_menuBarItems, 3) -- File, Options and Help are live during a battle, so a player can save, load, quit or open the options from the battlefield.
arms.note: The same arm is missing on the campaign map (crates/l2-game/src/screens/map.rs's table). Saving mid-battle is a question nobody has answered: Screen_HandleInput has no 0x29 arm and Menu_SaveGame does not test g_battlePhase.

arms.what: FIELD 7 OF 7 -- THE MULTIPLAYER CHAT LINE, and the only field that is not on a screen. Chat_Frame sets g_editActive from OUTSIDE Screen_HandleInput -- which is why the flag is cleared at the top of Screen_HandleInput only `if (g_chatTimer < 1)` -- commits to DAT_00553E80 at 64 characters and draws the line over whatever is underneath. Sixty-four characters, 470 pixels, kind 0, seeded empty.
arms.note: Opened by Chat_Toggle on VK_RETURN, and it takes over Return, End and every printable key on ANY screen while it is up: 0x0043600C refuses only screens 0x0A, 0x0D and 0x17. Missing because there is no multiplayer.

arms.what: A right release goes back to 0x29. It does NOT undo the box -- the live selection is left exactly as the last pointer motion made it, because the cancel is a screen change and nothing else.
g_screenId = 0x29; DAT_0053F238 = 0; DAT_0053E9AC = 1.
arms.why: See 0x00432221/dead-0x28-edge-scroll. Note it would UNPAUSE the battle, which is the only place other than the pause button that writes DAT_0053F238 to zero -- so whatever 0x28 was, leaving it started the fighting.

arms.what: 0x13 has a right-button test and an OK-corner test, either of which returns to the map. 0x12, one screen earlier, has NEITHER -- which is what made right-click-to-Decline look reasonable.

`if (g_battleHoverOnField == 0) g_screenId = 0x29` -- the pointer leaving the viewport ends the drag. Tested AFTER the two selection guards, so a release on the very frame the pointer leaves still commits.

The whole of Screen_FrameInput's 0x12 arm: the multiplayer sync latch DAT_00553FC8, and FUN_004BBEA7, a 20- or 30-second answer timeout. Both call Battle_Decline. FUN_004BBEA7 returns 0 unconditionally when g_multiplayer is clear, so IN SINGLE PLAYER THE ARM DOES NOTHING AT ALL and the prompt waits for ever.
arms.note: Missing because we have no multiplayer, not because it was overlooked. The waiting-for-ever half is reproduced and is correct.

arms.what: A right release sets DAT_00568470 = 0x1389 -- 5001, one past the limit Battle_CheckOutcome counts it up to -- so it SKIPS the outcome banner rather than dismissing it. The whole of 0x2B's arm.
The pointer on the outermost pixel of the screen scrolls the battle camera ONE cell, against the campaign map's two rows and one column. Map_ScrollStep's g_battlePhase == 2 half.
Screen_FrameInput's 0x28 arm opens with Map_EdgeScroll().
arms.why: Screen 0x28 is unreachable. Every immediate write of g_screenId in Lords2.exe was enumerated -- 212 `mov byte ptr [0x004EAC50], imm8` sites, values 0x00..0x45 -- and 0x28 is absent while 0x29, 0x2A and 0x2B are present; no decompiled function assigns it, and the indirect writes (g_screenIdSaved, g_menuPrevScreen) can only restore a value g_screenId already held.

arms.what: BattleMap_Click: the 160x160 panel at (480, 24), two pixels a cell over the whole 80x80 field. Left button with a selection, no oil selected and unpaused ORDERS to that cell; anything else, the right button included, puts the camera there. Reached from Screen_FrameInput's EPILOGUE, so it is live on 0x29, 0x2A and 0x2B alike.
Hotspot_Test(0x1E0, 0x1C0, &DAT_004DC710, 5) -- the five 32x32 buttons in a row at (480, 448). This record is the hit test; the five actions are five records of their own.

Arriving at page 4 SEEDS the field with the name you already have: both hotspot arms that open it -- FUN_00432B05's hotspot 2 and FUN_00432CC8's hotspots 3 and 5 -- run `Edit_Begin(&g_options, 0x10, 0xC0, 0); Edit_RecomputeLength();` immediately after setting g_setupPage = 4.

AND THE ASYMMETRY IS REAL: arriving at page 4 from page 5 or page 6 does NOT re-seed, because those arms set the page and nothing else. So a name typed on the way in through the campaign chooser survives the round trip and a name typed before going out to the title menu does not.

VK_RETURN's SECOND half -- the window procedure calls Edit_Confirm and then this. Opens the chat line if g_multiplayer is set and the screen is not 0x0A, 0x0D or 0x17, giving it a 5000-frame life; pressing it again sends the line as Net_SendCommand(6, 0) and closes it.
arms.note: Missing because there is no multiplayer. Recorded because it explains why Enter is NOT free on any screen in the original, which is the thing a reimplementation gets wrong: our screens spend Enter on activate, confirm and dismiss in five places.

arms.what: VK_END's SECOND half, and it is genuinely odd: Chat_Close clears g_chatTimer AND g_saveLoadConfirm, so pressing End after Enter on the save box CANCELS THE PENDING SAVE. The two counters are cleared by one function because chat and the save box are the only two things Return arms, and nothing separates them again.
arms.note: Reachable in single player -- neither half is guarded on g_multiplayer -- so this is a real key a person can press on a real save box, not a multiplayer-only arm. Missing because our save is immediate and has no latch to cancel; a save that took 150 frames the way SaveLoad_Tick's does would need it.

arms.what: PAUSE. Toggles DAT_0053F238 with a bitwise NOT, so it flips between 0 and -1. Battle_Start seeds it to 0xFFFFFFFF, so A BATTLE STARTS PAUSED and the first thing a player does is press this.

RETREAT -- Ui_OpenConfirm(12) 'Retreat from field?', or Ui_OpenConfirm(11) 'Surrender castle?' when this is a siege and the local player owns army B. Both callbacks reach FUN_0043BE65, which is Battle_AutoResolve and the return to the campaign. Guarded on g_battleChoiceOwner == 1.

Siege only, garrison only, castle level 3 or more, once per battle: FUN_00496B9F clears a 7x4 patch of cells flagged 0x40, writes surface 3 over it, adds 4 to both siege scores and rebuilds the pathfinding. On a field battle it enqueues message 0x6E and does nothing else.
arms.note: The BUTTON and its four guards are reproduced; FUN_00496B9F's rules are the siege agent's and are stubbed to the once-per-battle latch.

arms.what: CHARGE -- FUN_0047A76D puts every one of the local player's figures of troop type under 7 into free pursuit and halts its unit, which switches the every-500-frame reform off. Guarded by DAT_0055322C, so it fires ONCE in a battle.
arms.note: Not Order_ChargeNearest (0x0048C8AF), which is the AI's and also clears the withdraw flag and the figures' targets.

arms.what: Ui_OpenConfirm(9) 'Autocalc battle?'. Yes runs FUN_0043BE65 -- Battle_AutoResolve, which reads the CAMPAIGN records and never Battle_WriteBackCasualties, so every man killed so far is unkilled and the result is computed from the armies as they walked on.
A left press inside the viewport records the anchor cell and the anchor pixel and takes the screen to 0x2A. Gated on DAT_00568964 == 1 (input armed by Battle_Start) and g_battleHoverOnField.

The release, classified by FUN_00479CF7 into three: moved 25 pixels or more on either axis is a BOX and commits with FUN_0043C247(player, 1, ...); barely moved over one of your own men NUDGES THE BOX OUT BY EIGHT PIXELS each way and commits that, so a click picks a 16-pixel square; barely moved over nothing DOES NOTHING AT ALL and in particular does not clear the selection. The commit runs FUN_00478987, which allocates a new unit when the selection is not exactly one whole unit -- so a box drawn round half a unit SPLITS it.

The release test is `(g_mouseLeftReleased || g_mouseLeftDoubleClick) && g_screenId == 0x2A`, so a double click commits an open box exactly as a release would. Not a verb of its own: Windows sends WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK INSTEAD OF the second WM_LBUTTONDOWN, so without this the second click of a fast double click would leave the drag open with no press to end it.
arms.note: This is the second reader of g_mouseLeftDoubleClick that C61 predicted and crates/l2-game/src/input.rs denied. Hotspot_Test's kind-2 widgets are a third reader and are not an arm.

arms.what: While the button is down and the pointer has moved, FUN_0043C247(player, 0, ...) clears and re-boxes the selection LIVE. The 0 is what stops it regrouping units on every pointer motion.

A left press on one of the banners in the right column DROPS that figure from the selection (FUN_0043C4C6) -- it does not select it. The layout is one of three from DAT_004D31F4 by how many you hold, and only the first FIFTY are clickable whichever layout is up.

A right release CLEARS THE WHOLE SELECTION (FUN_0043C55C). Refused inside the overview panel -- x >= 0x1E1 && 0x18 <= y <= 0xB7 -- and note the off-by-one: the panel starts at 0x1E0, so its leftmost column deselects.
arms.note: This is the arm the project's 'right click exits' habit would have replaced with a way out of the battle. C61's second pattern.

arms.what: A left release on ground that holds none of your own men, with something selected and the battle unpaused, is an order: FUN_0043C634 plays a troop cry and calls BattleUnit_Order(currentUnit, cell, hoverEnemy, hoverWoodland, 0).

0x2A's ladder runs FUN_0043C57D as its second guard, so the order arm is live during a drag as well as on the field. In practice FUN_0043BF07 consumes the release first and this never fires; it is recorded because a change to the order of the two would make it fire, and because 'the same function on a second screen' is exactly what C61 found nobody counts.

H and V re-issue the player's current unit an order AT ITS OWN POSITION with BattleUnit_Order's sixth argument set to 1 or 2, which stores 0 or 1 in unit +0x09. Formation_ComputeRect (0x0048A1C9) reads that byte in one line -- `if (field_0x9 == 1) g_formationCols = 2` -- so the two keys are LINE and COLUMN and nothing else touches the byte.
arms.note: Settles docs/battle.md section 1's 'unnamed and untraced' for unit +0x09.

arms.what: Ctrl and 1..9 store the current selection into DAT_00553400 + (key - '1') * 0x18. The window procedure latches VK_CONTROL into DAT_004DF3A8 and its digit arm calls a DIFFERENT FUNCTION depending on it.

Keys 1..9 recall a stored selection and PUT THE CAMERA ON IT -- the function ends by scanning for the first selected figure and setting the viewport corner seven cells above and left of it. Nine slots (VK 0x31..0x39); Battle_Start clears ten.

The first thing Screen_FrameInput does on EVERY screen: a right release inside a 48x48 box round the message scroll dismisses it and SWALLOWS THE CLICK, so it never reaches the screen's own arms. A battle can raise messages (the siege gate button enqueues three of them), so this is reachable here.
arms.note: Not the battlefield's own arm -- it is every screen's, and is recorded under this group because a battle is where it was noticed.

arms.what: Battle_CheckOutcome and FUN_004782C5 both count DAT_00568470 up once a frame; past 5000 the banner gives way to Battle_WriteBackCasualties and Battle_ReturnToCampaign(1). Not an input arm; recorded because the skip above is one and is meaningless without it.

Battle_UpdateHover recomputes the five hover globals every frame: on-field, the cell, its surface, whether it is woodland, and whether the occupant is a friend, a picked friend or an enemy. Two of the three order arms read nothing else.
arms.note: One clause is reproduced CORRECTED rather than as found -- see docs/bugs.md B69, the stale figure index.

arms.what:
Player_SetHuman -- where a typed name stops being a keystroke: `g_realms[p].isHuman = 1; g_playerNames[p].occupied = 1; Str_Copy(0x53F1E0, &g_playerNames + p * 0x2C, 0x1F);`. THIRTY-ONE bytes out of the settings block into the name array, and the player index IS the realm index -- the same argument selects both.

The AI half of the same array is a different width and a different source: Eng_Seek(7, realm.lord) and SIXTEEN bytes copied. L2.eng group 7 is 'The Knight, The Baron, The Countess, The Bishop, No player', and the index is the LORD, not the realm and not the colour.
arms.note: g_playerNames is a save block of its own (g_saveBlocks[2] = {0x00553D50, 264} = 6 x 0x2C), which is why ours is on Game beside realm_colour rather than on Kingdom: the lockstep digest is hash_of(kingdom) and a name cannot change a number.

arms.what: F4 adds one hit to figures 1..20. A cheat, gated on DAT_0053F684 == 1.
The left and right arrow keys step g_debugSelectedMan down and up through 0..80, which is the figure the debug panel prints. UNGATED -- the only one of the four that is.

F2 cycles DAT_00568960 through 0, 1, 2, which picks between BattleDebug_Panel and two other overlays. All three draw only when DAT_0055402C is set, which is F3, which is gated on the debug flag DAT_0053F684 -- so the developers' panel is off in a shipped game and F2 alone cannot turn it on.
F3 toggles DAT_0055402C, which is what makes the three battle overlays draw at all. Gated on DAT_0053F684 == 1.

WM_CHAR's WHOLE ARM is Edit_TypeChar(ch) -- 0x00401A20 -- with no test of g_screenId, so every printable character a person types anywhere in the game goes into the one edit buffer. Whether it LANDS is g_editActive's business, not this arm's.

THE CHARACTER SET, exactly, in the chain's own order: space always; , . ? ! only when the field's kind is 0; - always; 0-9 always; a-z always; A-Z always, LOWER-CASED by 0x004011B0 when the kind is not 0; 0x80-0x9A, 0xA0-0xA7 and 0xE1 always. Everything else is dropped in SILENCE -- no beep, no message -- and that includes the apostrophe, the ampersand, every bracket and all of 0xA8-0xE0. A person typing O'Neill gets ONeill.
arms.note: Ours arrives as Event::Text rather than Event::KeyDown, which is the same split Windows makes: WM_KEYDOWN carries a key and WM_CHAR carries a character. It has to be, because Key::Char is folded to upper case for the hotkeys and a name typed through it would come out RICHARD.

arms.what: Battle_Frame's cursor ladder for 0x28..0x2A: seven leaves over four cursor kinds -- 0 arrow, 4 move, 5 attack, 6 select. An enemy under the pointer beats everything; 0x2A is always the arrow; with a selection in hand a pointer OUTSIDE the field still shows the move cursor as long as it is above y 184, which is the overview panel, where a click really does order.

DAT_004DDBB0[1], the thumb down at (372, 116), hotspot id 0 -> Battle_Decline, which is Battle_AutoResolve and the report. The table holds exactly these two records: g_sliderWidgets begins 48 bytes on at 0x004DDBE0, and the count DAT_00554408 is 2 when g_battleChoiceOwner == 1 and 0 otherwise.
DAT_004DDBB0[0], the thumb up at (332, 116), hotspot id 1 -> FUN_0043B593 -> Battle_Start. It RAISES THE BATTLEFIELD; it does not settle the battle.

FIELD 1 OF 7 -- THE LORD'S NAME. Screen_HandleInput's g_setupPage == 4 arm: `g_editActive = 1; Edit_RecomputeLength(); Chat_Timeout(); if (g_messageGroup == 0 && DAT_0055CD78 == 0) Edit_Commit(&g_options, 0x1F);`. The commit runs EVERY FRAME the page is up rather than on a button, and the two guards are a message box and an open drop-down over the page.

The limits are Edit_Begin's: SIXTEEN characters, 192 pixels, kind 0. The destination is g_options + 0 (0x0053F1E0), the persisted settings block, whose name field is 31 bytes and defaults to 'Player1' -- so the commit width (31) and the edit width (16) are different numbers and the smaller one is what a person meets.
arms.note: This is the field a player reported missing: 'I can't type my name in the start menu?'

arms.what:
FIELD 2 OF 7 -- THE SAVED GAME'S FILE NAME. Screen_HandleInput's arm is `else if (g_screenId == '5' || g_screenId == '6')`, ONE arm for both screens, so the original lets a person type the name of the game they want to LOAD as well as the one they want to save. SaveLoad_Tick builds the path out of the edit buffer either way -- `Str_Copy(0x4EA130, 0x4EAD60, 0xC); Path_AddExtension(...)` -- and never out of the highlighted row; clicking a row is what puts a name INTO the buffer.

Edit_Begin's limits here are EIGHT characters, 160 pixels, KIND 1 -- a DOS 8.3 name, so A-Z is lower-cased and , . ? ! are refused, the game supplying .sav, .svb or .sva itself.
arms.note: Two of the three limits are reproduced and the eight is not: our saves are .l2sav files in %APPDATA% and saves::MAX_NAME is 64. Holding a person to eight characters on a filesystem that has not had that limit since 1995 is superstition rather than fidelity -- the same line this module already draws about the scroll clamp. The 160-pixel limit still bites first.

arms.what: FIELD 3 OF 7 -- the front end's own load box, g_setupPage == 3. The same field as 0x004BA9C8/saveload-name with the same limits and the same destination buffer (DAT_004EA130, eight characters, kind 1), reached by FUN_00432CC8's hotspot 2, which also picks the extension by game mode: .sav single player, .svb multiplayer client, .sva multiplayer host.
arms.note: Missing because our SetupPage::Load is still a shell that draws three empty recesses -- it has no file list and no field. The screen 0x35/0x36 version of the same box is built.

arms.what:
FIELD 4 OF 7 -- THE LETTER YOU WRITE TO ANOTHER LORD, and the longest field in the game: `g_editActive = 1; Edit_RecomputeLength(); Edit_Commit(&g_diploLetterDraft + (g_diploKind * 5 - 5) * 0x28, 199);`. Two hundred characters, and the PIXEL limit is passed as 10000, which is fifteen screens wide and therefore no limit at all -- the only field in the game with none.

One arm, four buffers: g_diploKind 1..4 each index their own 200-byte slot at 0x0053F2B8, 0x0053F380, 0x0053F448 and 0x0053F510, and Diplo_OpenCompliment and its three neighbours each Edit_Begin their own. Counted as ONE arm because it is one guard and one computed destination.
arms.note: The diplomacy agent's screen. Recorded here because the enumeration found it, and it is the field most likely to be missed by someone building screen 0x1A from the painters -- the letter has no plate of its own.

arms.what: FIELD 5 OF 7 -- the multiplayer custom game's name, g_setupPage == 8: `g_editActive = 1; Edit_RecomputeLength(); Edit_Commit(&DAT_00553E80, 0x40); Str_ToLower(&DAT_00553E80);`. Sixty-four characters and then LOWER-CASED WHOLESALE by 0x00401246 after the commit -- which is a second, cruder lowering than the kind-1 filter's, applied to a kind-0 field.
arms.note: Missing because there is no multiplayer, not because it was overlooked.

arms.what: FIELD 6 OF 7 -- the same field on the multiplayer skirmish page, g_setupPage == 11. Byte-for-byte the same three statements as 0x004BA9C8/mp-custom-name, under a different page guard, which is why it is a second arm and not the same one.
arms.note: Missing because there is no multiplayer.

arms.what: When the local player did not own the choice, any click, right-click or key settled the battle by the standing policy.
arms.why: Battle_ChooseSettlement writes a widget count of 0 for a bystander, so the prompt has no widgets and no exit but the multiplayer timeout. In a single-player game the state cannot arise at all.

arms.what: Enter took the field.
arms.why: As above. The window procedure's Enter arm is FUN_0043600C, a text-field commit.

arms.what: Escape declined the battle.
arms.why: No key reaches screen 0x12 in the original. The window procedure's Escape arm calls Menu_Quit or sets DAT_005AEB68 = 1 and never touches the prompt.

arms.what: A right release on the take-the-field prompt ran Battle_Decline. Screen 0x12's arm has no right-button test of any kind.
arms.why: 'Right click exits' generalised from the screens where it is true. C61 found it by enumeration and this is its removal.

arms.what: Escape and Enter dismissed the battle report.
arms.why: 0x13's arm is a right-button test and Ui_OkButtonClicked. No key.

arms.what: Escape closes the save/load box.
arms.why: SaveLoad_Cancel (0x00434308) is the cross widget and nothing reaches it from the keyboard.

arms.what: Up and Down scroll the file list by one row of three.
arms.why: The original scrolls that list from the two arrow widgets and from nothing else. KEPT because a thirty-name list with no keyboard is awkward; note that Left and Right, which this screen also spent on the list, have been GIVEN BACK -- they are Edit_Left and Edit_Right, and a screen that spent them on a list left a person unable to move the caret in the one place the game has one.

arms.what: Enter or Space activates the highlighted item.
arms.why: As above. NARROWED by the name field: on page 4 the field takes Space as a character, because that is what it is, so this arm no longer fires there. Enter still does, and in the original Enter on page 4 is Chat_Toggle and does nothing in single player.

arms.what: Down moves the highlight to the next item.
Escape is the page's Back button, or leaves the front end from the title page.
arms.why: The window procedure's Escape arm is Menu_Quit when DAT_0052AF94 == 3 and `g_backOut = 1` otherwise; neither knows what page the front end is on.

arms.what: I opens crate::screens::index, our own list of every screen.
arms.why: A development affordance, and index is marked as ours already. NARROWED by the name field: on page 4 the letter I is the letter I.

arms.what: Up moves the highlight to the previous item.
arms.why: The original's front end has no keyboard at all -- see the group note. KEPT: a menu a person cannot drive from the keyboard is worse, not more faithful.
